chunks: Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār narrated from him, peace be upon him, who said:
A man may apply whatever oil he wishes, so long as there is no musk, no ambergris, no saffron, and no wars in it, before he performs ghusl for ihram.
He said: “And do not perfume a garment for your ihram with incense.”

key_terms.دُهْنٍ: oil or ointment used for anointing
key_terms.زَعْفَرَانٌ: saffron, used here as a fragrant substance
key_terms.عَنْبَرٌ: ambergris, a scented substance used in perfume
key_terms.لِلْإِحْرَامِ: for entering the state of ihram
key_terms.وَرْسٌ: wars, a yellow plant dye or scented substance
key_terms.يَدَّهِنُ: applies oil or ointment to oneself

ai.seo_question: Can a person use oil or perfume clothing before entering ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about preparation for ihram. It permits using oil before ghusl for ihram as long as it does not contain fragrant substances such as musk, ambergris, saffron, or wars, and it also forbids perfuming the ihram garment with incense.
